instructions.question: What sentiment does this Albanian Facebook comment on the Kosovo public health institute's COVID-19 post express: positive, neutral, or negative?
instructions.rule: Negative needs an explicit marker: horror or despair words, fed-up complaints, insults or curses, saying the institute lies or inflates the numbers (including jokes like 'admin, stop your hand'), or angry blame of the government. A sad topic (deaths, rising cases, maskless citizens), a pointed question, a proposal or a COVID doubt without such a marker is neutral; when torn between neutral and negative, choose neutral. Positive covers praise, thanks, blessings, relief or good news about recoveries, and hopeful encouragement. Town pride and off-topic congratulations are neutral.

neutral.what: Calm, playful or reasoned comments: questions, data requests, calculations, speculation, advice, proposals, criticism of citizens without insults, teasing friends about their town, jokes about delays or lab staff, tags, condolences.
examples: Pse ka Mitrovica Verit nuk po jepni Rezultate hiq !? (Why aren't you giving any results for North Mitrovica!?)
Koka qu sot heret ai i laboratorit (The lab guy got up early today)
Askund nuk mbajne distancat, askund nuk vendosin maskat (Nowhere do they keep distance, nowhere do they wear masks)
neutral.cues: hahaha, tagged names, pse (why), a ka (is there), duhet (should), hajde ma gjall (come on, livelier), kampion (champion), ngushllime (condolences), numbers
neutral.not_for: Comments with horror words, insults, curses, or claims of lies or inflated numbers are negative.

positive.what: Praise, thanks, blessings, relief that cases are falling, good news about recoveries, hopeful encouraging appeals.
examples: Asllan A Haxholli A ka lajm mat mir, 35 t'sherum (Is there better news, 35 recovered)
Shyqyr qeky nxeht e nali pak viusin se ke tu na shkatrru a (Thank God this heat has slowed the virus a bit, it was ruining us)
Perhajr edhe Juve (Blessings to you too)
positive.cues: bravo, ju lumtë (well done), faleminderit (thank you), shyqyr (thank God), lajm i mirë (good news), mir asht (it's good), t'sherum (recovered), mashallah, perhajr (congratulations/blessings)
positive.not_for: Sarcastic praise is negative. Condolences, 'Prishtina kampion' (Prishtina champion), 'Urime libralizimi i vizav' (congratulations on visa liberalisation) and recovery forecasts are neutral.

negative.what: Horror, despair, being fed up, insults, curses, accusing the institute of lying or inflating numbers, angry blame of the government.
examples: 15 te vdekur, tmerr. (15 dead, horror.)
kurr ska mu ba mir me ket popull budall (It'll never get better with this stupid people)
Mos rreni ma shum se kerkush sosht ka u kqyr mo kto prralla (Stop lying, nobody watches these fairy tales any more)
Hahahahahahha oo Admin Nale doren ‍♂️ (Hahaha, admin, stop your hand)
negative.cues: tmerr (horror), mjerim (misery), kjamete (catastrophe), boll keq (bad enough), na lodhet / u lodhum (worn out), na murren nqaf (you're killing us), budall / bosa (stupid / empty-headed), qija nanen (curse), rreni / rrene (lying/lies), prralla (fairy tales), dyshime (suspicions), nuk osht real (not real), nale doren (stop your hand), deshtu (failed), e hupi kontrollen (lost control)
negative.not_for: Reasoned arguments, proposals, and gentle jokes about delays or lab staff are neutral.
